conviction_note: Q3 revenue was pre-guided (~17% cc) a week before quarter end and consensus sits on it, so the print turns on the FY low-20% cc guide and the Q4 it implies (~15-20% cc), where peer evidence (Deckers' HOKA slowdown and sales cut, Nike's North America wholesale growth) leans negative. Against that sit a short position that nearly doubled since August to 9.8% of shares, upside-paid skew (-2.18) and a known tariff-refund headline. impact_sum is -0.7 while the scaled number is +0.4 (p_up 52 x abs 10): the findings lean slightly negative on fundamentals, positioning leans slightly positive, and the sign itself is close to a coin flip on a name that moves 6-20% on guidance.
bar: Revenue: Q3 2026 net sales ~CHF 928m (~+17% on Q3 2025's CHF 794.4m). The company guided 'about 17% constant-currency growth' at its 2026-09-22 investor day (https://www.tradingnews.com/news/on-holding-30-usd-gaps-above-29-usd-as-ivnestor--day-sets-22-percent-ebitda-margin-goal ; https://www.webull.com/news/15626288604382208). Consensus is CHF 928.28m per https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/on-holding-aktie-steigt-1-mrd-dollar-ruckkauf-und-wachstumsziele-bis-2029 (labelled USD there, but it matches the CHF base) and $1.14B per https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/ONON, which agree at ~0.81 CHF/USD. The company's own Aug-11 FY range of CHF 3.47-3.56bn at spot (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001858985/000185898526000018/a26q2-ex993xpressrelease.htm), less H1 of CHF 1,682m, implies H2 reported growth of +16% to +22%, about equal to constant currency. So FX no longer separates reported from cc growth in H2, and 17% cc is roughly CHF 928m reported. The revenue bar is therefore sourced (company guide plus two agreeing estimates). The EPS bar is DISPUTED: $0.37 (earningswhispers snippet in search) against $0.50 consensus / $0.52 whisper (earningswhispers page). The gap is roughly the size of the Q3 tariff refund, so EPS-based findings are capped small. FY guide: low-20% cc growth, gross margin >= 65.0%, adjusted EBITDA margin 19.5-20.0% (6-K above).
positioning_check: Short interest (FINRA via https://equibles.com/stocks/onon/shortinterest, read 2026-11-09): 32.91M shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 9.8% of shares outstanding, 3.10 days to cover. That is up from 27.89M (09-30), 23.00M (09-15) and 17.32M (08-14), so the short nearly doubled after the August guide cut. Equibles' model estimates 30.56M for 10-30 (-7%), not yet published; FINRA publishes it 11-10. Free float is smaller than shares outstanding (Class B held by founders), so the share of float is above 9.8%. This is building and moderately crowded, not extreme. Skew_25d -2.18 vol points (upside paid), put/call OI 0.75, event-implied move 8.77%. Tape: +4.36% over 5d, +4.87% over 20d, -26.8% from the 52-week high, +18% since the 08-11 print per earningswhispers, and roughly $32 on 10-27 to $37.07 now.

findings.finding: On guided Q3 2026 to about 17% constant-currency net sales growth at its 2026-09-22 investor day, eight days before quarter end. Consensus (~CHF 928m / $1.14B, about +17% reported) sits right on that guide, so the reported-quarter revenue has little room to surprise; On has historically cleared its own near-term guides, but in Q2 2026 it missed consensus (CHF 850.3m vs 881.4m).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Confirmed prints: 2025-11-12 Q3'25 beat and raised, +18-25% (https://www.schaeffersresearch.com/content/news/2025/11/12/on-holding-stock-soars-after-another-stellar-quarter); 2026-03-03 strong Q4 but 2026 guide below consensus, -6.1% close per baseline; 2026-05-12 Q1 beat (26.4% cc), sales guide reiterated and margins raised, -0.6% per baseline; 2026-08-11 Q2 sales miss and FY guide cut, -20.3%. Quarter beats without a guide raise have paid nothing.
findings.why_not_priced: It largely is priced: a guide given eight days before quarter end, with consensus sitting on it, leaves only the size of the beat open. If the market expected a large beat, consensus would sit above 17% and the stock would not still be 27% off its high.
findings.independence: https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/on-holding-liefert-starken-ausblick-und-genehmigt-aktienruckkauf-uber-1-mrd-dollar (same investor-day event, a different outlet) and https://www.webull.com/news/15626288604382208 (same event). Not independent of each other.

findings.finding: FY2026 guide arithmetic: Q1 +26.4% cc (CHF 831.9m), Q2 +21.6% cc (850.3m) and Q3 ~+17% cc put nine months at ~21.5% cc. A 'low-20%' FY on 2025's CHF 3,014m therefore needs Q4 growth of ~15% (for 20%) to ~23% (for 22%). With wholesale sell-in deliberately throttled and Q3 decelerating 4-5 points a quarter, the FY guide is at risk of being narrowed to the low end or cut; that, rather than Q3, is the line the stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has driven every large reaction: guide cut on 2026-08-11, -20.3%; first 2026 guide below consensus on 2026-03-03, -6.1%; guide raise on 2025-11-12, about +20%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the guide was cut once and the stock fell 20%. What is not visibly priced is a second trim. A market braced for one would show put-paid skew, but skew is -2.18 (upside paid) and the stock is up ~15% in two weeks. Management's stated expectation that Q4 grows faster than Q3 (BofA summary, https://www.investing.com/equities/on-holding) is the counterweight and is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: Q1 figures from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001858985/000185898526000014/a26q1-ex991xpressrelease.htm (a different document). FY2025 CHF 3,014.0m from https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260303925083/en. The Q3 ~17% cc figure shares a source with finding 1.

findings.finding: Deckers (HOKA) reported on 2026-10-22, after On last spoke: HOKA +6.8% to $677.2m, company DTC -1.8% (comparable DTC -6.4%), domestic sales -0.4%, the FY27 sales outlook cut to $5.700-5.725bn with HOKA now high-single-digit growth, and the CEO citing 'a challenging consumer environment'. DECK fell ~5% on it. This is a direct premium-running peer decelerating in the US channel where On's Americas grew only 13% cc in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No On print has followed a peer cut directly. On fell 20% in August 2026 on a US-wholesale-led miss, the same channel.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the read-through was public for two weeks and ONON still rose ~15% from late October, so the market has chosen to treat On as different (APAC +55% cc and EMEA +20% cc in Q2). If the market had priced a read-through, ONON would have tracked DECK down after 10-22. Net of the rest of the company: Americas is the region at risk, while APAC and EMEA would need to slow sharply for the total to miss, so this is sized as a proxy.
findings.independence: Stock reaction from https://ground.news/article/deckers-outdoor-slides-after-revenue-guidance-falls-short-of-expectations-deck-nyse (a different source). This is a proxy: no On document confirms the transmission.

findings.finding: Nike's Q1 FY27 (reported 2026-10-01, quarter to Aug 31) grew in North America, and its wholesale decline came from Greater China, not North America. This fits Nike regaining US wholesale shelf space in running, the channel On says it is deliberately under-shipping.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. Jefferies' 2025 downgrade thesis (retailer orders shifting back to Nike) preceded On's 2026 wholesale deceleration.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is five weeks old and broad. It is filed small because no source ties Nike's NA growth to running or to On's accounts.
findings.independence: https://ng.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/jefferies-downgrades-on-holding-on-slowing-growth-rising-nike-competition-2061388 is the same thesis, dated 2025. This is a proxy.

findings.finding: On expects up to $65m (up to CHF 53m) of US tariff refunds in Q3, booked to gross profit and excluded from guidance. Against a ~CHF 928m quarter that is up to ~570bp of gross margin and roughly the gap between the two EPS consensus figures in circulation ($0.37 vs $0.50), so the headline EPS and gross margin will likely print a 'beat' against any estimate that excludes it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No On history. Peer precedent: Deckers on 2026-10-22 raised EPS guidance with about $0.52 of refunds but cut sales, and the stock fell ~5%. The refund was noise next to the sales guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The refund itself is disclosed and priced. What is not settled is the bar: the EPS consensus is split, so the first headline may read as a large EPS beat. If every estimate already carried the refund, the sources would agree on the EPS.
findings.independence: The Q2 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001858985/000185898526000018/a26q2-ex993xpressrelease.htm) states that the outlook excludes tariff refunds expected in H2. The CEO said refunds would be reinvested rather than passed on (Reuters via https://www.itiger.com/news/2616343057), which limits any path to the guide.

findings.finding: Short interest nearly doubled after the August guide cut, from 17.3M shares (08-14) to 32.9M (10-15), 9.8% of shares outstanding and 3.1 days to cover. The stock has since rallied ~15% in two weeks and skew pays for upside (-2.18), so a print that merely holds the FY guide forces covering into the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2025-11-12 a beat and raise moved the stock about +20%; on 2026-05-12 a print with an unchanged sales guide moved it -0.6%. Squeeze behaviour on this name is not documented.
findings.why_not_priced: The short is public, but its size relative to the move matters: 33M shares against ~10M of average daily volume. The recent rally may already be covering (Equibles' model estimates -7% at 10-30). If the short had already covered, the 10-30 FINRA figure would show it; that figure is unpublished until 11-10.
findings.independence: The baseline skew -2.18 (upside paid) is a different source and points the same way.

findings.finding: The board authorised On's first share buyback on 2026-09-22: up to $1bn of Class A shares through December 2029, about 8% of the ~$12bn market cap. The Q3 release and call will be the first disclosure of whether and how fast it is being used.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The investor day that announced it, alongside 2029 targets, moved the stock +7.6% to +12.8% on 2026-09-22.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorisation is priced. Its execution pace is unknown ('authorizations are not obligations', tradingnews), and an aggressive start would be new.

findings.finding: Reported growth should converge with constant currency in Q3. The company's own Aug-11 FY range at spot (CHF 3.47-3.56bn) less H1 (CHF 1,682m) implies H2 reported growth of +16% to +22% on H2 2025's CHF 1,538m, against H1 reported growth of 14.5%/13.5% vs 26.4%/21.6% cc. The headline 'net sales +~17%' would be the first reported acceleration in a year, even though cc growth slows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history on this line. The FX gap was a talking point in the Q2 miss coverage (13.5% reported).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at CHF ~928m already reflects it, so this is a headline-optics item and not an estimate gap. If FX had re-widened since August, the CHF consensus would sit below 17% growth, and it does not.
findings.independence: USD/CHF in the 0.81-0.82 range in September 2026 (https://www.poundsterlinglive.com/history/USD-CHF-2026), versus a 2026 high of 0.8207 on 07-29, is consistent with a stable dollar.

findings.finding: Zalando (On's European online partner) reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-03: revenue +5% to EUR 3.174bn, B2C +2.8%, a swing to a net loss, and the FY outlook confirmed at the lower half of 12-17% growth. That is a soft European online fashion backdrop, though Zalando says it is betting on sports.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a week old and broad. It is filed small because no source gives On's share of Zalando, and On's EMEA grew 20.5% cc in Q2, far above Zalando.
findings.independence: https://english.aawsat.com/fashion/5205645-zalando-reports-higher-growth-third-quarter-bets-sports (sports as a growth bet; partly offsetting). This is a proxy.

findings.finding: Circana: US running footwear dollar sales grew 13% in H1 2026, against +1% for total footwear and +6% for performance footwear. The category On sells in is still growing double digits, so On's Americas slowdown is more channel management and share than demand.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It covers H1 and predates the Q2 miss's market reaction aftermath. It is filed as the broad series that the Deckers proxy must be read against.
findings.independence: Cuts against finding 3 (Deckers); both are filed, and Deckers is the more recent.

outside_window.finding: Amer Sports (Salomon footwear) reports Q3 2026 on 2026-11-17. That is a premium running/outdoor peer read, but it lands after the exit.

baseline_tension: The skew (-2.18, upside paid), the short build and the two-week rally lean up, while the guidance-arithmetic and peer findings lean down. The findings sum slightly negative (-0.7), against the option market and positioning, so p_up was held at 52 rather than below 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): Q3 pre-guided beat cut from +0.5 to +0.3, because in-line or beat quarters without a guide raise moved -0.6% and -6.1% on this name.
Rule 2 (one-offs): tariff refund cut from +0.5 to +0.3, because the Deckers precedent showed the refund to be noise next to the sales guide.

Rule 7 (positioning, crowded short and skew against negatives): guidance-risk finding cut from -1.5 to -1.2 and Deckers read-through from -1.0 to -0.8; short interest was looked up first (9.8% of shares out, 3.1 DTC, rising).
Rule 6 (bar): revenue bar confirmed by the company guide plus two agreeing estimates; the EPS bar is disputed ($0.37 vs $0.50), so the EPS-dependent refund item stays capped small.

'Reaction history built from wrong events': the baseline history was rebuilt from confirmed prints (two of the eight baseline events were not prints); abs_move_pct kept at 10, above the 8.77 implied, per the understatement lesson.
Left standing: positioning, buyback, FX, Zalando, Circana and Nike sizes unchanged; p_up and abs_move unchanged.
